message.content: ATP synthase (also known as Complex V) is the enzyme that produces ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in mitochondria. It uses the proton gradient generated by the electron transport chain to drive the synthesis of ATP. Protons flow back into the mitochondrial matrix through the F₀ channel of ATP synthase, causing rotation of the enzyme’s rotor subunits. This mechanical rotation is coupled to conformational changes in the catalytic F₁ head, which sequentially binds ADP and Pi, releases inorganic phosphate, and then releases newly formed ATP. In short, ATP synthase converts the energy stored in the proton motive force into chemical energy stored in ATP, the primary energy currency of the cell.
